_note: FL10 fragment. 'domains' restates D1, D2, D6, D7, D8 and D9 with the lifecycle findings of FL10 (ranges unchanged). Every flag index read by a scene-meta gate is also used by another scene group or by the engine, so by plan 4.1 rule 7 each one is a proposal, not a record; flags is empty on purpose.

D1.name: scene scratch
D1.lifecycle: ClearSceneState zeroes flags $0000-$000F at every scene load: STX $eventFlags with X = $0000 (16-bit, ROM bytes a2 00 00 / 8e 00 0a at 253273 / 253291) writes bytes $0A00-$0A01; its single call site is ExecuteSceneTransition (252507). OpenInventoryScreen pushes the same word, zeroes it for the overlay (the overlay exit flag is flag $0000) and pops it on close (191788-192094). The bytes are inside the save block, so a save and a load carry them, but the next scene load zeroes them again. The same index means different things in different scenes. A few scripts read the bytes as a whole: ir1F_plate_gate_opener (bits 1-4 of $0A00), mu66_rama_spirits (the $0A00 low byte equals $FE) and dm3F_switch / dm3F_mine_collapse_trigger (byte $0A01 used as a laborer counter).
D1.access: COP $CC-$D3 (byte and word forms), SetFlagRaw/TestFlagRaw/ClearFlagRaw, direct LDA/STA $eventFlags and $0A01.

D2.name: story / world events
D2.lifecycle: Part of the save block $0A00-$0BFB. Scripts set them, and a few scripts clear them (for example $96, $F4); no scene load clears a D2 bit except flag $FF (bit 7 of $0A1F), which ClearSceneState and the inventory overlay clear and set again after setup.
D2.access: COP flag opcodes, the *Raw helpers (actor-parameter indices: laborers $A0-$A3, necklace stones $98/$99, statues $F8-$FD, orbs $F2/$F3), scene-meta gates (D9).

D6.name: dungeon kill flags
D6.lifecycle: Global = WRAM-relative wramFlags index + $0400 (index = enemy number). ClearAllWramFlags zero-fills $0A80-$0A9F (16 words, LDX #$0000 as a2 00 00 at 46285); it is called once each from WorldMapController (238336, world-map entry), st68_kara (438261) and sp58_red_eye (426502). game_over_sequence clears the same 32 bytes inline on a real game over (54988-55002); a revive keeps them. The bytes are inside the save block. No reset at an ordinary scene change was found.
D6.access: SetWramFlag (SetDungeonKillFlag), CheckEnemyDefeatedFlag (inline AND $wramFlags,Y), COP $D8 (index = enemyNum), direct LDA $0A9F in gw88_tomb_dark_space.

D7.name: boss reward / ability unlock
D7.lifecycle: Save block. $0500-$0507 are the bits of byte $0AA0 (Offset100 helpers mask the index to 3 bits; boss_clear_reward_handler uses six rows, $0500-$0505). $0510-$051F are the 16 bits of the abilityBitmask word at $0AA2 (TestFlag_0510 = characterForm*4 + slot; the traced set is $0510-$051A). The rest of the range is not flag storage in the code that exists: $0AA6, $0AAC, $0AB0 and $0AB2 are 16-bit state words (D8) and $0AA4-$0AA5, $0AA8-$0AAB, $0AAE-$0AAF have no access in extracted/.
D7.access: The *_Offset100 helpers, TestFlag_0510, direct reads and writes of abilityBitmask ($0AA2).

D8.name: non-bitfield gates
D8.lifecycle: Items, character form, gems and other bytes of the save block that scripts test (FL40 extends the tool). Four 16-bit state words sit inside the flag-array tail: $0AA6 (script state: SwitchCase selector in dc2F_adrift, plate id in UseItem plate handlers), $0AAC globalScriptIndex (Dark Space layout variant, hieroglyph slot index), $0AB0 jewelsCollected, $0AB2 (Dark Space layout variant, saved copy of $0AAC).
D8.access: COP $D4-$D7 (items), SwitchCase on $0AD4/$0AA6, direct reads and writes.

D9.name: scene-meta gates
D9.lifecycle: A flag index read from a scene-meta command stream (SceneCmd_Branch, opcode $13 <flag> <label>) at scene load. TestFlagRaw masks the index to a byte, so only flags $0000-$00FF can gate. The 18 gates of 11 records use nine indices, all D2: $21, $4C, $70, $7B, $7E, $88, $96, $B3, $F4. A set flag skips to the unique $14 label (possibly in another record); a clear flag continues with the next command.
